from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Vectors are arrows, not just single points.", "They represent both magnitude and direction.", "Picture a robot starting at origin (0,0).", "It moves to position (3,2).", "The vector [3,2] marks this displacement."]
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Vector: Movement in Space", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create axes for visualization
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 3, 1], axis_config={"include_numbers": True}).scale(0.5)
        # Apply layout fixes from issues
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'C3', 'F5', scale_factor=0.55)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        self.add(dot)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        arrow = Arrow(start=axes.c2p(0, 0), end=axes.c2p(3, 2), color=YELLOW, buff=0)
        self.play(Create(arrow))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED))
        robot = Circle(radius=0.15, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1).move_to(axes.c2p(0, 0))
        self.add(robot)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        self.play(robot.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(3, 2)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        vector_label = MathTex(r"\\vec{v} = [3, 2]").set_color(PURPLE)
        # Apply layout fix from issues
        self.place_at_grid(vector_label, 'C2', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Write(vector_label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Vector addition combines two distinct movements.", "Use the tip-to-tail method for vectors.", "Place the start at the previous tip."]
        self.setup_layout("Vector Addition: Combining Forces", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define Vectors
        v1 = Vector([2, 1], color=WHITE)
        v2 = Vector([1, -2], color=WHITE)
        
        # Use Assets
        ruler = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg").scale(0.5)
        pencil = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/pencil.svg").scale(0.3)
        
        # Animation Group
        v1_group = VGroup(v1, ruler.copy().next_to(v1, UP, buff=0.1))
        v2_group = VGroup(v2)
        vectors_group = VGroup(v1_group, v2_group).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(vectors_group, 'A4', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(Create(v1_group), Create(v2_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        # Move v2 tail to v1 tip
        target_pos = v1.get_end() + (v2.get_end() - v2.get_start()) / 2
        self.play(v2_group.animate.move_to(target_pos))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#0000FF"))
        result_vec = Arrow(start=v1.get_start(), end=v2.get_end(), color=BLUE)
        self.add(pencil.move_to(result_vec.get_end()))
        self.play(Create(result_vec), pencil.animate.move_to(result_vec.get_end()))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Basis vectors i and j span space.", "Combine them to reach any point.", "Every location is a linear combination."]
        self.setup_layout("Linear Combinations: The Basis of Space", lecture_lines)
        
        # Grid setup for visualization
        grid = NumberPlane(x_range=[-3, 3], y_range=[-3, 3], axis_config={"include_numbers": False})
        # Use Asset as requested
        icon_grid = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg")
        
        # Applying layout improvements based on feedback
        self.place_in_area(grid, 'C2', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(grid)
        self.place_at_grid(icon_grid, 'B2', scale_factor=0.3)
        self.add(icon_grid)

        i_vec = Vector(RIGHT, color=WHITE)
        j_vec = Vector(UP, color=WHITE)
        
        # Align with origin of the grid (0,0)
        origin = grid.c2p(0, 0)
        i_vec.shift(origin - i_vec.get_start())
        j_vec.shift(origin - j_vec.get_start())

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(i_vec), FadeIn(j_vec))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Scale i and j to form point (2, 1)
        i_scaled = Vector(2 * RIGHT, color="#FFFF00")
        j_scaled = Vector(1 * UP, color="#FFFF00")
        
        i_scaled.shift(origin - i_scaled.get_start())
        j_scaled.shift(origin + 2 * RIGHT - j_scaled.get_start())
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(i_vec.copy(), i_scaled), ReplacementTransform(j_vec.copy(), j_scaled))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        point = Dot(grid.c2p(2, 1), color="#FF00FF")
        self.play(Create(point))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Linear Algebra: Vectors as Spatial Guides
outline.target_audience: High school students or introductory undergraduate students

sections.title: Defining the Vector: Movement in Space
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a vector as an ordered pair representing magnitude and direction, distinct from a single point. Visualize this as an arrow starting at the origin (0,0) and ending at a specific coordinate.
sections.example: A 'Robot Dog' starting at the charging station (0,0) moves to position (3, 2). The vector v = [3, 2] describes this displacement.

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication: Stretching the Path
sections.content: Explain how multiplying a vector by a scalar (a real number) changes its length but keeps its direction (or reverses it). Use a scaling animation to show the vector growing or shrinking along the same line.
sections.example: The 'Robot Dog' runs twice as fast, effectively doubling its displacement vector: 2 * [3, 2] = [6, 4].

sections.title: Vector Addition: Combining Forces
sections.content: Introduce vector addition using the 'Tip-to-Tail' method. Visually demonstrate placing the start of the second vector at the tip of the first to find the final resultant position.
sections.example: The 'Robot Dog' first moves [3, 2] to find a ball, then moves [1, -3] to find a bone. The total displacement is [3+1, 2-3] = [4, -1].

sections.title: Linear Combinations: The Basis of Space
sections.content: Explain how any point in a 2D plane can be reached by combining the basis vectors (i = [1,0] and j = [0,1]). This serves as the foundation for defining span and coordinate systems.
sections.example: Think of the 'Robot Dog' moving on a grid. To reach any point (x, y), it simply moves 'x' units along the x-axis and 'y' units along the y-axis, representing the combination: x[1,0] + y[0,1].
